questions.text: Tell me about a time when you had to lead a team through a difficult project. What was your approach?
follow_up_questions: How did you handle team members who were resistant to your direction?
What would you do differently if you faced the same situation today?

star_hints.situation: Describe the project context, team size, and what made it difficult.
star_hints.task: Explain your role and what you were responsible for delivering.
star_hints.action: Detail the specific steps you took to lead the team — communication, delegation, motivation.
star_hints.result: Share measurable outcomes: delivery timeline, team morale, business impact.

questions.text: Describe a situation where you had to make an unpopular decision. How did you handle the pushback?
follow_up_questions: How did you communicate the decision to stakeholders?
Looking back, do you think it was the right call?

star_hints.situation: Set the scene — what was the context and why was the decision controversial?
star_hints.task: What was your responsibility in making this decision?
star_hints.action: How did you communicate, justify, and implement the decision despite opposition?
star_hints.result: What happened as a result? Did the decision prove correct over time?

questions.text: Give me an example of a time you mentored or coached a junior team member to improve their performance.
follow_up_questions: How did you tailor your coaching style to that individual?
What was the most rewarding part of the mentoring experience?

star_hints.situation: Who was the person and what performance gap existed?
star_hints.task: What was your goal in mentoring them?
star_hints.action: What specific coaching techniques, feedback sessions, or resources did you provide?
star_hints.result: How did their performance improve? Any measurable change?

questions.text: Tell me about a time you had to influence people without having direct authority over them.
follow_up_questions: What tactics did you use to build buy-in?
How did you handle someone who refused to cooperate?

star_hints.situation: Describe the cross-functional or peer situation.
star_hints.task: What outcome were you trying to achieve?
star_hints.action: How did you build relationships, present your case, and gain alignment?
star_hints.result: Did you achieve the goal? What was the impact?

questions.text: Describe a time when you had to set a vision or direction for your team. How did you get everyone aligned?
follow_up_questions: How did you handle team members who had a different vision?
How did you measure whether the team was aligned?

star_hints.situation: What was the context — new project, team restructure, strategic shift?
star_hints.task: What vision did you need to establish and why?
star_hints.action: How did you communicate, involve the team, and create shared ownership?
star_hints.result: How did alignment manifest? What was the outcome?

questions.text: Tell me about a time you worked on a high-performing team. What made it successful?
follow_up_questions: What was your specific contribution to the team's success?
How would you replicate that team dynamic in a new environment?

star_hints.situation: Describe the team, project, and context.
star_hints.task: What was the team's goal and your role?
star_hints.action: What behaviors, practices, or dynamics made the team effective?
star_hints.result: What did the team achieve? What was the measurable impact?

questions.text: Describe a situation where you had to work with a difficult team member. How did you handle it?
follow_up_questions: Did the relationship improve over time?
What did you learn about yourself from that experience?

star_hints.situation: Who was the difficult person and what made them challenging?
star_hints.task: What did you need to accomplish together?
star_hints.action: How did you approach the relationship — direct conversation, empathy, escalation?
star_hints.result: What was the outcome for the project and the relationship?

questions.text: Give me an example of a time you had to put the team's needs above your own preferences.
follow_up_questions: How did you feel about making that sacrifice?
Would you make the same choice again?

star_hints.situation: What was the team situation and what personal preference did you set aside?
star_hints.task: What was the team trying to achieve?
star_hints.action: What did you do and how did you communicate your decision?
star_hints.result: How did it benefit the team? What was the outcome?

questions.text: Tell me about a time you had to collaborate with a remote or cross-functional team.
follow_up_questions: What tools or processes did you use to stay aligned?
What was the biggest challenge of working remotely/cross-functionally?

star_hints.situation: Describe the team composition, location, and project.
star_hints.task: What was your role and the shared goal?
star_hints.action: How did you communicate, coordinate, and overcome distance/silo challenges?
star_hints.result: What did the team deliver? How effective was the collaboration?

questions.text: Describe a time when you helped a struggling team member without being asked.
follow_up_questions: How did you notice they were struggling?
How did they respond to your help?

star_hints.situation: Who was struggling and what were the signs?
star_hints.task: What did you want to achieve by helping?
star_hints.action: What specific help did you offer — time, knowledge, emotional support?
star_hints.result: How did it impact them and the team's overall performance?

questions.text: Tell me about the most complex problem you've ever solved at work. Walk me through your process.
follow_up_questions: What data or information did you use to diagnose the problem?
Were there any solutions you considered but rejected? Why?

star_hints.situation: What was the problem and why was it complex?
star_hints.task: What was your responsibility in solving it?
star_hints.action: Walk through your analytical process — how did you break it down, gather data, evaluate options?
star_hints.result: What was the solution and its impact?

questions.text: Describe a time when you had to solve a problem with limited resources or information.
follow_up_questions: How did you decide when you had enough information to act?
What would you have done differently with more resources?

star_hints.situation: What was the constraint — time, budget, data, people?
star_hints.task: What needed to be solved despite the constraints?
star_hints.action: How did you prioritize, improvise, or find creative solutions?
star_hints.result: What was the outcome? How effective was your solution?

questions.text: Give me an example of a time you identified a problem before it became critical. What did you do?
follow_up_questions: How did you convince others that the problem was worth addressing?
What early warning signs did you notice?

star_hints.situation: What was the potential problem and how did you spot it early?
star_hints.task: What was your role in addressing it proactively?
star_hints.action: What steps did you take to prevent escalation?
star_hints.result: What was prevented? What was the impact of your early action?

questions.text: Tell me about a time when your first solution to a problem didn't work. What did you do next?
follow_up_questions: How did you stay motivated after the initial failure?
What did you learn from the failed approach?

star_hints.situation: What was the problem and what was your initial approach?
star_hints.task: What were you trying to achieve?
star_hints.action: How did you pivot — what did you learn from the failure and what did you try next?
star_hints.result: Did the second approach work? What was the final outcome?

questions.text: Describe a time you used data or analytics to solve a business problem.
follow_up_questions: What data sources did you use?
How did you present your findings to non-technical stakeholders?

star_hints.situation: What was the business problem and why was data needed?
star_hints.task: What analysis were you responsible for?
star_hints.action: What data did you gather, how did you analyze it, and what insights did you find?
star_hints.result: What decision was made based on your analysis? What was the impact?

questions.text: Tell me about a time you had to explain a complex technical concept to a non-technical audience.
follow_up_questions: How did you know your audience understood?
What analogies or visuals did you use?

star_hints.situation: Who was the audience and what was the complex concept?
star_hints.task: What did you need them to understand or decide?
star_hints.action: How did you simplify, use analogies, visuals, or storytelling?
star_hints.result: Did they understand? What decision or action followed?

questions.text: Describe a situation where miscommunication caused a problem. How did you resolve it?
follow_up_questions: What could you have done to prevent the miscommunication?
How did you rebuild trust after the misunderstanding?

star_hints.situation: What was the miscommunication and what caused it?
star_hints.task: What needed to be resolved?
star_hints.action: How did you clarify, address the misunderstanding, and repair the situation?
star_hints.result: What was the outcome? What process changes did you make?

questions.text: Give me an example of a time you had to deliver difficult feedback to someone. How did you approach it?
follow_up_questions: How did the person react to the feedback?
What framework do you use for delivering difficult feedback?

star_hints.situation: Who needed the feedback and what was the issue?
star_hints.task: What outcome were you hoping to achieve with the feedback?
star_hints.action: How did you prepare, frame, and deliver the feedback constructively?
star_hints.result: How did they respond? Did their behavior change?

questions.text: Tell me about a time you had to present to senior leadership or executives. How did you prepare?
follow_up_questions: How did you handle tough questions from the executives?
What would you do differently next time?

star_hints.situation: What was the presentation about and who was the audience?
star_hints.task: What did you need to achieve with the presentation?
star_hints.action: How did you structure, prepare, and rehearse? How did you tailor to executives?
star_hints.result: What was the outcome? Did you achieve your goal?

questions.text: Describe a time when you had to actively listen to understand someone's perspective before responding.
follow_up_questions: What techniques do you use to ensure you're truly listening?
How did active listening change your response?

star_hints.situation: What was the conversation and why was listening important?
star_hints.task: What did you need to understand?
star_hints.action: What active listening techniques did you use — paraphrasing, questions, silence?
star_hints.result: How did your understanding change? What was the outcome?

questions.text: Tell me about a time you had to adapt quickly to a major change at work. How did you handle it?
follow_up_questions: What was the hardest part of adapting to the change?
How did you help others adapt as well?

star_hints.situation: What was the change — restructure, new technology, strategy shift?
star_hints.task: What did you need to adapt to and why was it challenging?
star_hints.action: How did you approach the change — learning, mindset shift, seeking help?
star_hints.result: How well did you adapt? What was the outcome?

questions.text: Describe a time when your priorities changed suddenly. How did you manage the shift?
follow_up_questions: How did you communicate the priority change to your team?
What did you have to deprioritize and how did you decide?

star_hints.situation: What caused the sudden priority change?
star_hints.task: What new priority needed your attention?
star_hints.action: How did you re-plan, communicate, and execute the shift?
star_hints.result: What was the outcome? How did you manage competing demands?

questions.text: Give me an example of a time you had to learn a new skill or technology quickly to complete a project.
follow_up_questions: What resources did you use to learn quickly?
How did you apply the new skill under pressure?

star_hints.situation: What skill was needed and what was the timeline?
star_hints.task: What did you need to deliver using this new skill?
star_hints.action: How did you learn — courses, mentors, practice, documentation?
star_hints.result: How well did you apply the skill? What was the project outcome?

questions.text: Tell me about a time you worked in an ambiguous situation with unclear requirements. How did you proceed?
follow_up_questions: How did you decide when to ask for clarification vs. proceed independently?
What assumptions did you make and how did you validate them?

star_hints.situation: What was ambiguous — requirements, goals, ownership?
star_hints.task: What did you need to deliver despite the ambiguity?
star_hints.action: How did you clarify, make assumptions, and move forward?
star_hints.result: What did you deliver? How did stakeholders respond?

questions.text: Describe a time when a project you were working on changed direction significantly. How did you respond?
follow_up_questions: How did you manage the emotional impact of the change?
What did you do to get the team re-energized?

star_hints.situation: What was the original direction and what changed?
star_hints.task: What was your role in navigating the change?
star_hints.action: How did you pivot — re-planning, communication, team motivation?
star_hints.result: What was the outcome of the new direction?

questions.text: Tell me about a time you had a conflict with a colleague. How did you resolve it?
follow_up_questions: What did you learn about yourself from that conflict?
How has your approach to conflict changed since then?

star_hints.situation: What was the conflict about and who was involved?
star_hints.task: What did you need to resolve?
star_hints.action: How did you approach the conversation — direct, empathetic, structured?
star_hints.result: Was the conflict resolved? What was the relationship outcome?

questions.text: Describe a time when you had to mediate a conflict between two team members.
follow_up_questions: How did you remain neutral during the mediation?
What would you do differently if the conflict escalated?

star_hints.situation: What was the conflict between the team members?
star_hints.task: What was your role as mediator?
star_hints.action: How did you facilitate the conversation and find common ground?
star_hints.result: Was the conflict resolved? How did it affect team dynamics?

questions.text: Give me an example of a time you disagreed with your manager's decision. How did you handle it?
follow_up_questions: How did you decide when to push back vs. accept the decision?
What was the outcome of your disagreement?

star_hints.situation: What was the decision and why did you disagree?
star_hints.task: What did you want to achieve by raising your concern?
star_hints.action: How did you communicate your disagreement — respectfully, with data, privately?
star_hints.result: What happened? Did the decision change? How did it affect your relationship?

questions.text: Tell me about a time when you had to deal with a customer or stakeholder complaint. How did you handle it?
follow_up_questions: How did you manage your emotions during the complaint?
What process changes did you make to prevent similar complaints?

star_hints.situation: What was the complaint and who was the stakeholder?
star_hints.task: What did you need to resolve?
star_hints.action: How did you listen, acknowledge, and address the complaint?
star_hints.result: Was the stakeholder satisfied? What was the outcome?

questions.text: Describe a time when competing priorities between teams caused tension. How did you navigate it?
follow_up_questions: How did you get both teams to agree on a solution?
What governance or process did you put in place to prevent future conflicts?

star_hints.situation: What were the competing priorities and which teams were involved?
star_hints.task: What needed to be resolved and what was at stake?
star_hints.action: How did you facilitate alignment — meetings, escalation, compromise?
star_hints.result: What was agreed upon? What was the business outcome?
